claims.text: Rapidly quenched equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is initially single-phase.
Rapid quenching produces minimal intrinsic chemical short-range order in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Annealing at 600–700°C for 1–10 hours followed by slow cooling promotes short-range order in CoCrFeMnNi relative to rapid quenching.
Thermally induced short-range order forms nanometric clusters.
The short-range-order clusters form preferentially at or near grain boundaries.
Short-range-order clusters alter the grain-boundary chemical environment.
Grain-boundary-localized short-range order reduces grain-boundary cohesion.
Short-range-order clusters act as preferential crack-nucleation sites under low-temperature loading.
Thermally aged specimens containing short-range order will have lower fracture strain than the rapidly quenched baseline.
Thermally aged specimens containing short-range order will have lower toughness than the rapidly quenched baseline.
Thermally aged specimens will show increased intergranular crack propagation relative to the rapidly quenched baseline.
The predicted embrittlement will be stronger under cryogenic loading than under room-temperature loading.
The rapidly quenched, minimally ordered baseline has higher ductility and toughness than the aged condition.
The proposed effect applies from cryogenic to room temperatures while the alloy retains an overall single-phase state.
Secondary microstructural evolution during thermal treatment may influence the measured effects attributed to short-range order.
